title: Editing inherited scene's hierarchy breaks animations
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.stable.mono.official [5b4e0cb0f]

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 31.69 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I have a base scene with a specific node hierarchy, including an AnimationPlayer. I then create a derived scene inheriting from it and create animations on various nodes in the scene. If I then change the hierarchy of those nodes in the base scene, all animations referencing them are broken and have to be fixed by manually redirecting all tracks across all animations. You can work around it by manually using the unique name path with `%` but then if you ever use the keyframe button next to a property, it will create a new track instead of using the unique name one.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a base scene with a child node and a grandchild node under it, plus an AnimationPlayer node
- Create a derived scene inheriting from it and create some animation referencing a property of the grandchild node
- Save and return to the base scene, reparenting the grandchild to the root node (making it a direct child)
- Return to the derived scene to find the animations are broken and must be repaired manually

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

In `base_scene.tres`, reparent `ColorRect` to `BaseScene` as a direct child and the `test` animation in `child_scene.tres` will break.

[InheritedAnimationIssue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29116835/InheritedAnimationIssue.zip)
